critical_code_review_comments: MessageCard is becoming too broad — 400+ lines with many props (comments, variants, approval, template, creatives, evolution, custom). Splitting responsibilities (e.g., MessageCardFooter, MessageCardEvolutionActions) would prevent the whole-view crash we just hit.

The recently added Evolution integration relies on passing 5+ props (isCustom, onRemoveCustom, canUseEvolution, evolutionConfig, onEvolutionSend) from FlowView down to MessageCard — consider a MessageContext provider so adding a new feature doesn't silently forget to destructure a prop.

server.py /evolution/send raises 500 when the target server_url is unreachable; the spec wants {ok:false, status>=400, no crash}. Today httpx timeout/DNS errors land in the `except Exception` and become a 500. Suggest wrapping the connection errors into {ok:false, status:503, error:str(e)} so the UI can show a friendly aviso rojo without treating it as a backend crash (my test currently accepts both).

review_sign uses a hash of approval+edits+signer+now_iso. 'now_iso' is included inside the canonical payload AND stored separately, so the hash isn't actually a content fingerprint — re-signing the same content twice yields different hashes. Suggest splitting: content_hash (approval+edits+signer only) and storing signed_at alongside, so 'same content verified twice' is detectable.

rca_of_the_issue: Root cause of the MessageCard crash: during iter-4 E1 added five new props (isCustom, onRemoveCustom, canUseEvolution, evolutionConfig, onEvolutionSend) and passed them from FlowView (App.jsx:1149-1153) to MessageCard, but forgot to destructure them in the MessageCard function signature (App.jsx:733-741). React then read them as globals → ReferenceError. Additionally, showEvoSend/setShowEvoSend were referenced without a useState hook. Both are classic prop-drilling additions without updating the receiver. Fix applied: added the 5-prop destructure with defaults and the missing useState.
